entries.name: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
entries.description: Single Rust binary plus agent hooks that rewrite shell commands (git, pytest, ls, grep, ruff...) to compact filtered output, with raw-output recovery on failure
entries.license_status: mixed; the rtk-oss edition is Apache-2.0 only; no code copied
entries.agent_os_overlap: Workers run Claude Code or Codex, which accept PreToolUse hooks, so a hook could be installed per worker; but 94% of measured tool-result bytes already come from narrowed commands and distill's equivalent pipeline saved 0 bytes on them. Retry prompts already quote failing test output.

algorithms: store full output behind a hash and show a recall hint when a filtered command fails
tests_benchmarks: per-filter >=20% savings floor tested on captured real command-output fixtures

entries.integration: none now; possible later as a per-worker PreToolUse hook (rtk-oss edition) if replay shows a large unfiltered git/pytest share

risks.maintenance: very active, many contributors, fast-moving filters
risks.license: full binary includes BUSL-1.1 engine; the oss edition avoids it
risks.dependency_weight: third-party binary in every worker worktree; hook fires only on Bash calls

evidence.development_savings: none: adopting it is a hook config, but nothing to build or borrow today
evidence.runtime_savings: unmeasured here; README says bash-output bytes only, estimated as bytes/4. JetBrains SkillsBench on Claude Code measured +7.6% cost at low effort and ~0% at high effort; Quesma's 1,740-run Terminal-Bench 2.1 study found reported reductions did not become cheaper runs
evidence.quality: independent runs showed unchanged task quality; fixtures show filters keep failures and drop passing lines, but no later-use check exists
evidence.reliability: falls back to the raw command if a filter fails; propagates exit codes
evidence.security: hook rewrites every Bash command; it ships integrity checks (SHA-256 hook verification) and a trust model, not audited here
evidence.complexity: low to configure, high to audit 100+ filters
evidence.portability: Linux/macOS/Windows binaries; hooks for 18 agents incl. Claude Code and Codex

entries.rationale: Independent cost evidence is flat to negative and on our measured traffic 94% of bytes are already narrowed by the model's own commands, so there is little left to filter. Revisit only if a replay shows a large unfiltered git/pytest share.
provenance: web search found no r/OpenSourceAI thread; Reddit unreachable
revisit_when: replay of recorded tool results shows >15% of bytes from unfiltered git/pytest/ruff commands
a paired-run study on Claude Code shows net cost savings at equal effort
Agent OS runs its own agent loop

entries.name: Headroom
entries.description: Local context-compression layer (library, proxy, agent wrapper, MCP server) with a reversible compress-cache-retrieve store, JSON/code/prose compressors and optional output-token shaping
entries.license_status: Apache-2.0; model weights hosted separately, license not checked; no code copied
entries.agent_os_overlap: A proxy reachable through the worker's base-URL setting is the only route here that acts on Claude Code/Codex traffic without Agent OS owning the loop. The same results already failed our later-use check for lossy crushers and history rewrites cost 2-6% more than they saved.

algorithms: per-tool retrieval-rate as the quality signal for how aggressively to compress (compression_feedback.py)
hold out 10% of conversations as an unshaped control so savings are measured, not estimated
tests_benchmarks: benchmarks/index_proof_table.py: seeded offline proof table using provider tokenizer

entries.integration: none now; candidate offline replay of recorded tool results through compress() in library mode

risks.maintenance: fast-moving, commercial team offering, vendor perks banner
risks.quality: lossy compressors; recovery depends on the model calling the retrieval tool
risks.dependency_weight: Python package with Hugging Face model, SQLite store, learned telemetry and a proxy
risks.cache: rewriting tool results in history changes the prefix; cache mode only partly mitigates

evidence.development_savings: none yet; borrowing the retrieval-rate signal and holdout pattern is small
evidence.runtime_savings: first-party only: 21-57% on four seeded synthetic scenarios (README), higher on repetitive JSON/logs, small on prose; not measured on our traffic
evidence.quality: README accuracy table is N=100 with deltas inside the CI and tests prompts not coding tasks; one hands-on Copilot test found more tokens consumed because needed information was removed; our replay found lossy crushers removed text the model later used in 28-47% of reduced results
evidence.security: runs locally; proxy forwards provider keys and persistent stores of originals on disk
evidence.complexity: high: proxy, wrapper, MCP server, memory, learn command
evidence.maintenance: active, stars and trending badges but vendor-reported numbers
evidence.portability: Python/pip, Claude Code, Codex and 15 other agents via wrap or proxy

entries.rationale: It is the only candidate that could run as a drop-in proxy, but savings are first-party and synthetic, lossy reduction already failed our later-use check, and history rewrites risk the cache. Run the offline replay before any live trial.
provenance: web search found no r/OpenSourceAI thread; Reddit unreachable
revisit_when: offline replay of the 528 recorded results shows >10% bytes saved with <5% later-use loss
an independent paired coding-agent benchmark appears
Agent OS gains its own loop or a proxy layer

entries.name: TML (Tool Manifest Language)
entries.description: Compact line-based format and OpenAPI converter that describes API tools to LLMs with fewer tokens; a schema format, not a tool-output reducer
entries.agent_os_overlap: Tool schemas for Claude Code and Codex are defined by the CLIs and their MCP servers; Agent OS has no loop in which to send a .min tool block. The assignment called it a single-file tool-call verbosity reducer; the repo is a schema format with a CLI and studio UI.

tests_benchmarks: benchmarks/measure-tokens.js: token counts taken from Claude API input_tokens

entries.integration: none; would apply only to an own-loop adapter in adapters/http_api.py

risks.maintenance: experimental v0.1, single maintainer, last commit April 2026
risks.quality: models are trained on JSON function schemas; a custom format has no robustness evidence

evidence.runtime_savings: README claims 174 vs 769 tokens (77%) for 3 tools; benchmarks README shows 243 vs 1047; MCP comparison rows are character-based estimates
evidence.quality: 100% tool selection on 5 scenarios and 35 calls against one weather API with 3 tools; no baseline of hand-trimmed JSON or tool search
evidence.security: neutral; Studio server holds an API key in .env
evidence.portability: any text model, but not what CLI tool loaders accept

entries.rationale: It shortens tool schemas the CLIs define rather than tool results, rests on 3-tool, 5-scenario benchmarks with mixed estimated and measured numbers, and Agent OS has no loop to use it in.
provenance: web search found one Reddit post via a snapshot mirror (subreddit not confirmed, one comment); no independent benchmark
revisit_when: Agent OS builds an own tool-calling loop with a large custom tool list
independent benchmark compares it with JSON schemas and tool search

entries.name: Intel Adaptive Token Compressor
entries.description: Python library with a harness compressor (LLMLingua-2 over system prompt and context) and a tool compressor (predictor LLM selects tools, accumulate mode keeps the prefix cache stable)
entries.agent_os_overlap: Tool selection acts on the tools array an agent loop sends, which Agent OS does not own with Claude Code or Codex; the harness half is LLMLingua again (see PA-llmlingua) and is lossy.

algorithms: accumulate: union of predicted tools per conversation in append-only order so the tool block stays a prefix extension and the cache keeps hitting
per-compressor metrics for tokens, ratio and latency

entries.integration: none now; the append-only-tool-set idea can inform an own-loop adapter or per-role allowlists chosen once at worker start

risks.maintenance: first release 2026.2, weeks old, corporate sample library
risks.quality: source docstring says trailing-carrier placements fail on multi-turn agents; ~60% of turns change the predicted tool set
risks.dependency_weight: needs a Lingua model server and an external predictor LLM endpoint

evidence.runtime_savings: no published numbers in repo or docs; README says 'significantly reduce token usage'
evidence.quality: docstrings report internal findings (placement failures, prediction instability) with the referenced report not in the repo
evidence.reliability: has tests and health checks; not run here
evidence.security: sends task context to a predictor endpoint
evidence.complexity: high for what it saves: two model servers

entries.rationale: Tool selection needs a loop Agent OS does not own and there are no published numbers; the one idea worth keeping, append-only tool sets that protect the prefix cache, can be tested when an own-loop adapter exists.
provenance: web search found no independent evaluation and no r/OpenSourceAI thread
revisit_when: Agent OS runs its own agent loop with a large tool list
Intel publishes accuracy and token numbers for ToolCompressor
